root_cause.text: The powerpc pgtable fragment teardown path in pte_frag_destroy() freed a cached PTE-fragment folio without clearing the folio's active flag, because pte_free_defer() had introduced ACTIVE as a deferred-free marker but pte_frag_destroy() did not handle that state when pt_frag_refcount dropped to zero.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `folio_clear_active(ptdesc_folio(ptdesc));` immediately before `pagetable_dtor()`/`pagetable_free()` in `arch/powerpc/mm/pgtable-frag.c`, and the commit message explicitly states that `pte_free_defer()` “sets the active flag” while `pte_frag_destroy()` “simply call[s] pagetable_dtor() and pagetable_free(), meaning it doesn't clear the active flag,” causing the reported “Bad page state” with `flags: ... (active ...)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the active flag on a page-table folio before destroying and freeing it when the final PTE fragment reference is dropped.
intent_record.what: A call to folio_clear_active(ptdesc_folio(ptdesc)) was added inside the branch where atomic_sub_and_test(PTE_FRAG_NR - count, &ptdesc->pt_frag_refcount) evaluates true, immediately before pagetable_dtor(ptdesc) and pagetable_free(ptdesc).
intent_record.how: When the last PTE fragment reference is released and the page-table descriptor is about to be destroyed and freed, the associated folio now has its active flag cleared first. This prevents the folio from remaining marked active during teardown and ensures its state is consistent before deallocation.

grouping_result.intent: Clear the active flag on a page-table folio before destroying and freeing it when the final PTE fragment reference is dropped.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it clears the folio/page active flag in the PTE fragment teardown path before freeing when the last fragment reference is dropped, fixing the missing ACTIVE-state handling in pte_frag_destroy().

    powerpc: convert various functions to use ptdescs
    
    In order to split struct ptdesc from struct page, convert various
    functions to use ptdescs.
    
    Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20230807230513.102486-13-vishal.moola@gmail.com

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant teardown logic is fully shown in this snippet, especially `pte_frag_destroy()` and the deferred-free handling in `pte_fragment_free()`. The root cause is that deferred free uses the ACTIVE flag as a marker, but `pte_frag_destroy()` frees the underlying page-table folio without clearing/checking that marker first. In this commit, `pte_fragment_free()` clearly shows the ACTIVE-based deferred free path: `else if (folio_test_clear_active(ptdesc_folio(ptdesc))) call_rcu(&ptdesc->pt_rcu_head, pte_free_now); else pte_free_now(&ptdesc->pt_rcu_head);`. However, `pte_frag_destroy()` does not perform any analogous `folio_test_clear_active(...)` check before freeing when the fragment refcount reaches zero: `if (atomic_sub_and_test(PTE_FRAG_NR - count, &ptdesc->pt_frag_refcount)) { pagetable_pte_dtor(ptdesc); pagetable_free(ptdesc); }`. That means the vulnerable construct is present: the destroy path can directly destruct and free a cached PTE-fragment folio while ignoring the ACTIVE deferred-free marker. Therefore this version still has the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
